# Gobbly.io

> Gobbly.io is a free casual game for iPhone and Android where you roll a hungry little ball around colourful maps, eat the goal items before the timer runs out, and grow bigger with every bite. Made by Sultan of Niyyat.

- Google Play: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.sultanofniyyat.rollandgobble.game
- App Store: https://apps.apple.com/app/id6824868785

## Quick facts

- Price: Gobbly.io is free to download and free to play.
- Ads: There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. From level 4, a short full-screen ad can also appear now and then between levels and when you come back to the game.
- Purchases: Optional purchases are coin packs, booster bundles, a Gold Season Pass and a one-time Remove Ads. Every level can be beaten without buying anything.
- Offline: Yes. Every level works without Wi-Fi or mobile data. Ads, purchases and cloud saving need the internet.
- Opponents: Gobbly.io is a single-player game. There are no other balls in a level and no live opponents. The Weekly Contest and rankings are worked out on your phone, and there is no chat.
- Round length: about 1 to 3 minutes
- Age rating: rated 4+ on the App Store; the game is meant for players aged 13 and over
- Needs: Android 7.0 or newer or iOS 15 or newer

## Questions and answers

- [What is Gobbly.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/what-is-it/): Gobbly.io is a free casual game for iPhone and Android where you roll a hungry little ball around colourful maps, eat the goal items before the timer runs out, and grow bigger with every bite. You start each level as a small ball that can only eat little things, and every bite helps you grow until you can eat cakes, chairs and cars. It is free on the App Store and Google Play.
- [How do you play Gobbly.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-play/): Touch anywhere on the screen and drag: the ball rolls the way you drag. Lift your finger and it stops. Roll into food and things that are small enough and the ball eats them. Eat every item on the goal cards before the timer runs out to win the level.
- [Is Gobbly.io like Hole.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-is-it-different-from-hole-io/): It is the same family of game: you swallow things, grow bigger and can then swallow bigger things. The differences are that in Gobbly.io you are a rolling ball, not a hole, and you play single-player levels with a goal list and a timer instead of racing other players to be the biggest.
- [What can the ball eat, and why can't I eat that yet?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/what-can-the-ball-absorb/): The ball can eat anything whose size is the same as the ball's size or smaller. If something will not go in, the ball is not big enough yet: eat smaller things nearby, grow a size, and come back.
- [How do you grow faster in Gobbly.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-grow-faster/): Eat as many small things as you can in the first seconds, roll through crowded areas instead of chasing single items, and move up to bigger things as soon as you grow. Keep moving: empty ground wastes time.
- [How do you beat a hard level in Gobbly.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-beat-a-level/): Read the goal cards first, grow quickly on the small food, and only then go for the big goal items that need a high size. Use boosters on HARD and SUPER HARD levels, and keep away from bombs. Every level can be beaten without buying anything.
- [What are the most common beginner mistakes?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/beginner-mistakes/): The big ones are going for the big goal items before you are big enough, stopping on single items, going back over cleared ground, and rolling into bombs. Fix those and levels get much easier.
- [Who should play Gobbly.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/who-should-play/): Gobbly.io suits people who want a quick, easy, satisfying game: fans of Hole.io and other eat-and-grow games, people who play in short breaks, and anyone who likes clearing a full map. It is not for players looking for a story, deep strategy or live matches against other people.
- [Why are games like Gobbly.io so satisfying?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-satisfying/): Eat-and-grow games give you constant small rewards: every bite makes you visibly bigger, and a crowded map slowly becomes clean. Gobbly.io adds piles of food that pour into the ball and a goal list that ticks down, so there is always a "just a few left" moment.
- [Is Gobbly.io a relaxing game?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-good-for-relaxing/): Mostly, yes. The controls are simple, levels are short and there is no one else to fight, so it is easy to switch off and just roll around eating things. The timer adds a little tension, and harder levels ask for more focus.
- [Is Gobbly.io suitable for kids?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-ok-for-kids/): The game itself is simple and non-violent: a ball rolls around eating food and toys. It is rated 4+ on the App Store; the game is meant for players aged 13 and over. Parents should know about ads and purchases: There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. From level 4, a short full-screen ad can also appear now and then between levels and when you come back to the game. Optional purchases are coin packs, booster bundles, a Gold Season Pass and a one-time Remove Ads. Every level can be beaten without buying anything.
- [How long is a level, and is it good for short breaks?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-long-is-a-level/): A level of Gobbly.io takes about 1 to 3 minutes. Early levels are short and later levels get longer. That makes it a good fit for short breaks, commutes and waiting rooms.
- [Is Gobbly.io free?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-free/): Gobbly.io is free to download and free to play. There are optional reward videos you can choose to watch for extras such as more time, a heart or coins. From level 4, a short full-screen ad can also appear now and then between levels and when you come back to the game. Optional purchases are coin packs, booster bundles, a Gold Season Pass and a one-time Remove Ads. Every level can be beaten without buying anything.
- [How do you remove ads in Gobbly.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/how-to-remove-ads/): Tap REMOVE ADS on the ad break screen. It is a one-time purchase that switches off the ads between levels and when you open the game, for good. Buying anything else in the game switches them off too. Reward videos you choose to watch stay available.
- [Can you play Gobbly.io offline?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/can-you-play-offline/): Yes. Every level works without Wi-Fi or mobile data. Ads, purchases and cloud saving need the internet.
- [Is Gobbly.io multiplayer?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/is-it-multiplayer/): No. Gobbly.io is a single-player game. There are no other balls in a level and no live opponents. The Weekly Contest and rankings are worked out on your phone, and there is no chat.
- [Will Gobbly.io run on my phone?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/will-it-run-on-my-phone/): Gobbly.io runs on iPhone with iOS 15 or newer and on phones with Android 7.0 or newer. The download is about 90 MB. If the store shows the game for your phone, your phone is supported.
- [Will I lose my progress in Gobbly.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/saving-progress/): Your progress is saved on your phone automatically. On Android it is also saved in the cloud with Google Play Games, so it comes back on a new phone signed in to the same Google account. On iPhone there is no cloud save yet, so deleting the app deletes your progress. Remove Ads comes back on any phone with Restore Purchases.
- [What is an io game?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/what-is-an-io-game/): An io game is a simple, fast arcade game where many players share one arena, usually trying to grow bigger or survive longest, with very short rounds and one-touch controls. The name comes from Agar.io (2015), a browser game that used the .io web address ending; later games copied the name and the style.
- [What are the best games where you eat things and grow?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-like-it/): The best-known eat-and-grow games are Katamari Damacy (roll a sticky ball that grows), Hole.io (a hole that swallows a city), Donut County (a story game about a growing hole) and Agar.io (cells that eat to grow). Gobbly.io mixes the rolling ball idea with short timed levels and a goal list.
- [What are good games to play offline, without Wi-Fi?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/best-offline-games-no-wifi/): Good offline games are ones where every level lives on your phone, so nothing stops when the signal drops. Look for single-player games with levels or puzzles, not online matches. Gobbly.io is one: Yes. Every level works without Wi-Fi or mobile data. Ads, purchases and cloud saving need the internet.
- [What are the most satisfying games to play on your phone?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/best-satisfying-games-for-phone/): "Satisfying" games give you lots of small, visible results: a mess becomes tidy, things fit perfectly, or something grows with every touch. The main kinds are clean-up games, sorting games, eat-and-grow games and slicing or crushing games. Gobbly.io is an eat-and-grow game: piles of food pour into your ball and a full map ends up empty.
- [What are the best io games on mobile?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/best-io-games-on-mobile/): The best-known io games are Agar.io (eat cells to grow), Slither.io (a growing snake), Paper.io (claim territory) and Hole.io (a hole that swallows a city). They share one-finger controls and short rounds. Most of them match you against other players online.
- [What are eat-and-grow games?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/eat-and-grow-games/): Eat-and-grow games are games where you swallow things to get bigger, and getting bigger lets you swallow bigger things. You might be a hole, a ball, a cell or a snake. Gobbly.io is the ball kind: you roll around maps eating food and toys before the timer runs out.
- [What games are like Hole.io?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-like-hole-io/): Games like Hole.io are eat-and-grow games: you swallow things and grow until you can swallow the biggest objects. Some keep the online race against other holes; others turn it into levels. Gobbly.io is a level-based one where you play as a rolling ball.
- [Are there games like Katamari Damacy on phones?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-like-katamari-on-phone/): Katamari Damacy (Namco, 2004) is the classic game where you roll a sticky ball that grows by picking things up. On phones, the closest feeling comes from ball-based eat-and-grow games. Gobbly.io is one: you roll a ball that eats food and toys and grows through sizes, in short timed levels.
- [What can I play after Donut County?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-like-donut-county/): Donut County (2018) is a short, funny story game about a hole that swallows a town. If you want more of that swallowing, look at other eat-and-grow games: Hole.io for online rounds, Katamari Damacy for the rolling-ball classic, or Gobbly.io for hundreds of short levels with a growing ball.
- [What are good quick games for a short break?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/quick-games-for-short-breaks/): A good short-break game lets you start at once, finish something in a few minutes and stop without losing anything. Level-based casual games are the best fit. A Gobbly.io level takes about 1 to 3 minutes.
- [What are good relaxing games to unwind with?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/relaxing-games-to-unwind/): Relaxing games are simple to control, have no pressure from other players, and give gentle, steady rewards. Popular choices are sorting games, farming and building games, slow puzzle games and satisfying games. Gobbly.io is mostly relaxing, with a light timer that adds a little tension.
- [What are good games you can play with one hand?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/one-hand-games/): One-hand games are played in portrait mode with one finger: tapping, swiping or dragging. Good kinds are eat-and-grow games, runners, merge games and many puzzle games. Gobbly.io is fully one-finger: Touch anywhere on the screen and drag: the ball rolls the way you drag. Lift your finger and it stops.
- [What are good games for flights and long trips?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-for-flights-and-travel/): The best travel games work in airplane mode, do not drain the battery fast and come in short pieces you can pause between. Download them at home on Wi-Fi and test them in airplane mode before you leave. Gobbly.io works fully offline.
- [What are good casual games for adults?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/best-casual-games-for-adults/): Adults playing casual games usually want something easy to pick up, quick to finish and not demanding: puzzle levels, word games, sorting and satisfying games, and eat-and-grow games. Gobbly.io fits that: short levels, one finger, and a clear goal each time.
- [What makes a good puzzle-arcade game with levels?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/best-puzzle-arcade-games-with-levels/): Good level-based puzzle-arcade games start easy, get harder in waves, give a clear goal every level and let you win without paying. Gobbly.io mixes arcade movement (rolling and growing) with a puzzle side: choosing what to eat first so you are big enough for the last goal items.
- [What are good beat-the-clock games?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/beat-the-clock-games/): Beat-the-clock games give you a goal and a countdown. A good timer makes the last seconds exciting without feeling unfair. In Gobbly.io, you must eat every goal item before the timer reaches zero.
- [What kinds of rolling ball games are there?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/rolling-ball-games/): Rolling ball games come in a few kinds: tilt mazes, downhill runners, physics puzzles and eat-and-grow games. Gobbly.io is an eat-and-grow ball game: you drag to roll a ball that eats food and toys and grows through sizes.
- [What are fun games where you eat food?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/food-eating-games/): Food games range from cooking and restaurant games to eating games where your character gobbles everything in sight. Gobbly.io is the eating kind: Gobbly, a hungry ball, eats fruit, cookies, donuts, burgers, cakes and more, and grows with every bite.
- [What are ASMR games on mobile?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/asmr-games-for-phone/): "ASMR games" are phone games built around soothing sounds and satisfying visuals: crunching, popping, slicing, cleaning or sorting. Gobbly.io is not a pure ASMR game, but it shares the feel: food pops into the ball with little sounds, "+1"s and light vibration.
- [What is the difference between hyper-casual and hybrid-casual games?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/hyper-casual-vs-hybrid-casual/): Hyper-casual games are tiny, instant games with one simple action and almost nothing else. Hybrid-casual games keep that simple action but add progress to come back for: levels, boosters, collections and events. Gobbly.io is hybrid-casual.
- [What games work on phones with little storage?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-for-low-storage-phones/): For phones with little space, look for games under about 150 MB that do not download big extra packs after installing. Gobbly.io is about 90 MB and needs iOS 15 or newer on iPhone or Android 7.0 or newer.
- [Are there good games that need no login or account?](https://sultanofniyyat.github.io/gobbly-io/games-without-login/): Yes. Many single-player games let you play without creating an account: you open the app and start. Gobbly.io is one of them: no account, no name, no email. The game does not ask for an account, your name, your email, your contacts or your location. Two analytics services (GameAnalytics and Google Analytics for Firebase) and one ad service (Google AdMob) receive some device and game information, as the privacy policy explains.
